title: Exclude past/expired time slots from the availability list
tech: Primarily Node/TypeScript backend (the actual defect); one small, complementary frontend change
keyConstraints: Root cause, confirmed by reading both files in full: backend/src/validation/bookingSchema.ts already rejects a past start_at at booking-creation time (`.refine((value) => new Date(value).getTime() > Date.now(), { message: 'must be in the future' })`), but backend/src/services/availabilityService.ts's computeAvailableSlots -- which generates the slot list GET /availability returns -- has no reference to Date.now() or 'now' ywhere in the function. It computes free time purely from availability_rules/availability_exceptions/bookings for whatever date string it's given, with zero awareness of whether that date, or a given slot within it, has already passed. Two concrete symptoms: (1) requesting today's date returns slots earlier in the day that have already passed: (2) requesting any date in the past (e.g. last month) returns a full day of slots, all of which are unbookable. Both share the same root cause and the same fix location. The fix should exclude any candidate slot whose start is not in the future, mirroring bookingSchema.ts's own rule as closely as possible so the two checks stay consistent -- a slot that's offered by GET /availability should never then be rejected by POST /bookings for being in the past. All of computeAvailableSlots's interval math already operates in UTC epoch milliseconds internally (Interval.start/end are `number`, only converted to local-zone strings/ISO at the boundaries) -- adding a 'not in the past' constraint needs no timezone-conversion work and introduces no DST risk; it's the same category of operation as the existing rule/exception/booking interval handling already there, not a new one. Real design question, not just an implementation detail -- flagging for Architect rather than deciding here: should the cutoff be exactly Date.now() (mirrors bookingSchema.ts exactly, simplest), or should it include a small forward buffer (e.g. exclude anything starting within the next several minutes) to reduce the residual case where a slot is valid when listed but has tipped into the past by the time a customer finishes filling in their name/email/phone and submits? Note BookingWidget.tsx already re-fetches and shows a message on a 409 today (`slotTakenMessage`, worded for 'someone else took it' -- not perfectly accurate for 'time passed', but that copy nuance is out of scope here unless trivial to improve alongside this fix).
description: Fix GET /availability (backed by computeAvailableSlots) so it never returns a slot that's already in the past, or that will imminently become unbookable before a customer could realistically submit it. As a complementary, defense-in-depth measure (not a substitute for the backend fix, since the API can be called directly), add a min attribute to BookingWidget.tsx's date input so a customer can't pick a past date via the native date picker in the first place.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /availability never returns a slot whose start time is not in the future at the moment the request is served, consistent with (and never inconsistent with) bookingSchema.ts's own 'must be in the future' rule for POST /bookings

Requesting availability for a fully past date returns an empty slot list, not an error -- consistent with BookingWidget.tsx's existing 'no slots available' empty-state handling for a day with genuinely no availability
Requesting availability for today only returns slots that haven't already passed -- slots earlier in the day than the current time are excluded
BookingWidget.tsx's date input gets a min attribute preventing a past date from being selected via the native picker
Existing availability integration tests (test/integration/availability.test.ts) continue to pass; new test(s) cover a 'today, with some slots already in the past' case and a 'fully past date' case
npm test, npm run build, npm run lint, and tsc --noEmit all pass in both backend/ and frontend/
relevantFilePaths: backend/src/validation/bookingSchema.ts (existing 'must be in the future' rule -- read-only reference, the rule to stay consistent with)
frontend/src/pages/BookingWidget.tsx (add min attribute to the date input)
frontend/test/BookingWidget.test.tsx (extend if the min attribute needs coverage)
securityConsiderations: None new -- GET /availability is already public and read-only. If anything, this reduces incidental exposure of stale/irrelevant scheduling data (a full day of slots for a date that's already passed).
